Daily Briefings · Wednesday, November 11, 2026

Space & Defense Daily — Wednesday, Nov 11, 2026

The U.S.–Russia–Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi ended with a prisoner-exchange deal but no breakthrough, and Witkoff and Kushner head to Putin and Zelensky next; NATO jets twice failed to shoot down a drone that crossed Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia overnight; the SDA gave SpaceX a ~$10M study to link its lasercom with missile-warning networks as the Pentagon also lends $150M to Rocket Lab to ease the launch crunch.

← NewerThu, Nov 12, 2026All briefingsOlder →Tue, Nov 10, 2026
NATOEuropean UnionUnited StatesEuropean spaceGlobal space & defense

Top stories: The trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi ended without a breakthrough on ending the war, but they produced a large prisoner-exchange deal. U.S. envoys are due to meet Putin and Zelensky next. Overnight, NATO jets twice failed to shoot down a drone that crossed Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, and the Baltic states issued shelter alerts. In U.S. military space, SDA awarded SpaceX a study on bridging its lasers with missile-warning satellites, and the Pentagon committed a $150M loan to Rocket Lab as launch capacity tightens.

NATO

  • NATO fighters twice failed to shoot down a drone over northern Lithuania overnight, and one missile fell near Biržai. The drone went on through Latvia and Estonia into Russia, while shelter alerts sounded across the Baltics and Finland briefly restricted the eastern Gulf of Finland. (Euronews)
  • Lithuanian officials said four drones and dozens of smuggling-balloon radar tracks were recorded, and that a second NATO jet's missile run hit "technical difficulties." The country carrying out the air-policing mission will investigate. (LRT)
  • Allies are weighing the biggest overhaul of NATO force planning in at least 20 years. Under the draft Political Guidance, allies would plan forces for either a major European war or several crisis-management missions, rather than both at once. Agreement is targeted for February. (Politico Europe)
  • British police arrested a 41-year-old senior U.S. soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence, and the FBI called the case an espionage matter. (Defense News / Reuters)
  • Today, Rutte is at the Atlantic Future Forum aboard HMS Prince of Wales in Oslo, where ministers and industry are meeting over two days on Europe carrying more of its own defence. (NATO; Nordic Defence Watch)

European Union

  • In Bulgaria and Romania, von der Leyen announced €50M for a Black Sea Maritime Security Hub and €10M in search-and-rescue aid for each country. She said Bulgaria stands to get €3.3B from SAFE and that more than €20B is on offer in the second SAFE call. (Brussels Times)
  • Member states have until Nov. 30 to say how much they want to borrow in the €21.3B second SAFE round, and the Commission is pushing joint procurement with Ukraine. (2EU Brussels)
  • Rheinmetall signed a contract worth several hundred million euros for 20 Skyranger 30 air-defence systems for Belgium, to be integrated into its "Blue Dome." Deliveries start in late 2028. (Rheinmetall)

United States

  • The Space Development Agency awarded SpaceX nearly $10M to study integrating its proprietary laser links with missile-warning and tracking satellites, as the Space Force tries to bridge networks built on different optical standards. (SpaceNews)
  • The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital made a $150M conditional loan commitment to Rocket Lab to raise Neutron's flight rate, two weeks after a similar loan to Stoke Space. (U.S. Department of War)
  • Ars Technica says the two loans point to Pentagon worry about a launch crunch as SpaceX winds down Falcon. SSC now forecasts up to 249 medium- and heavy-lift national-security launches through the early 2030s. (Ars Technica)
  • Space Systems Command awarded Viasat an IDIQ contract with a $450M ceiling, including a $115M first task order, for the Space Data Network's mission operations center. The award was made in partnership with Golden Dome. (Air & Space Forces Magazine)
  • AST SpaceMobile disclosed that it expects about $100M from a subcontract to STR on a Space Force program to track airborne targets from orbit. (SpaceNews)
  • Ars Technica reports that Golden Dome faces a renaming and the likely loss of its space-based interceptors under the incoming Democratic Congress. Its FY26 reconciliation money has lapsed, and pending FY27 bills fund only a fraction of the $17B+ request. (Ars Technica)
  • The House voted 211–204 to send Rep. Massie's eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, which effectively shelves them for this Congress. (Breaking Defense)
  • SpaceX's classified USSF-627 Falcon 9 launch from Vandenberg slipped again. It now targets tonight, Nov. 11, with the window opening at 6:35 p.m. PT and a backup on Nov. 12. (SpaceX)
  • NASA picked eight companies, including SpaceX, Blue Origin and Lockheed Martin, to compete for up to $10B in CLPS lunar deliveries for its Moon Base, plus $1.3B in separate task awards. (Fortune)

European space

  • Britain's £2.4B Skynet wideband satellite decision has become a political fight over reports that Lockheed Martin UK beat incumbent Airbus. The MoD says "no final decisions" have been made, and analysts warn the outcome could affect UK participation in the Airbus–Thales–Leonardo space merger. (Breaking Defense)
  • The EU Space Act reached a deal in the European Parliament's ITRE committee, with a committee vote set for Nov. 19 and trilogues possible from December. (Table.Briefings)
  • France cleared Globalstar to launch and operate 54 next-generation direct-to-device satellites, with deployment starting next year. (SpaceNews)

Global space & defense

  • The Abu Dhabi talks closed after two days with no breakthrough, though Moscow and Kyiv confirmed a large prisoner swap. Witkoff and Kushner go to Putin in Moscow and Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday, and Kushner wants Europeans "added to the format." (BBC)
  • At the G7 in Paris, Ukraine's foreign minister pressed Rubio to speed up interceptor deliveries as Russia hammers the power grid. He said PURL deliveries and U.S. intelligence sharing continue. (Defense News / Reuters)
  • The U.S. moved at least 10 KC-135 tankers out of RAF Mildenhall over a reported Iranian threat and raised security to FPCON Charlie, and Britain insisted its bases are safe. (Defense News / Reuters)
  • China launched the Pathfinder astronomy satellite for its Tanyuan project on a Long March 2D from Jiuquan. It was China's 83rd space mission of 2026. (China Daily)
